item.text:
# 8B.10 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh, 2024

Bottom line: **No, not overall.** There were real short-term policy and administrative wins early in 2024, especially on procurement digitization, macro stabilization, and some targeted planning. But the year ended with a legitimacy collapse, coercive crisis management, and Hasina’s resignation and flight, so she was **not closer by year-end to a durable program** than she was at the start.

## Positive evidence

- **Bangladesh Receives $900 million World Bank Financing to Increase Economic and Urban Resilience for Sustainable Growth** | World Bank | 2024-06-21 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/21/bangladesh-receives-900-million-world-bank-financing-to-increase-economic-and-urban-resilience-for-sustainable-growth  
  Claim: The Bank said the package would support fiscal and financial-sector reforms, institutionalize e-GP, strengthen banking oversight, improve tax design, and fund resilience spending. This is strong evidence that a real policy program was being implemented, not just advertised. | Question IDs: 8B.10

- **Bangladesh: Second Reviews Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement and the Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility** | IMF | 2024-06-24 | https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/186/article-A001-en.xml  
  Claim: IMF said program performance was broadly on track and noted exchange-rate realignment, tighter monetary policy, a crawling peg, and tax/subsidy reforms. This is the clearest evidence of short-term macro course correction. | Question IDs: 8B.10

- **Inclusion of govt procuring agencies in e-GP mandatory** | Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority | 2024-03-06 | https://bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1446.html  
  Claim: BPPA said e-GP was mandatory for government procuring agencies and described it as improving transparency, efficiency, and competition. This is concrete administrative implementation and a real anti-discretion reform. | Question IDs: 8B.10

- **Advancing healthcare excellence: WHO's role in developing the first national medical education strategy in Bangladesh** | WHO Bangladesh | 2024-03-04 | https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh  
  Claim: The health ministry, with WHO support, launched a strategy based on workforce studies and a technical working group to improve curriculum, accreditation, faculty development, and digital transformation. This is evidence of evidence-based policy work inside the state. | Question IDs: 8B.10

- **Hasina reiterates call for China to help repatriate Rohingyas from Myanmar** | TBS News / UNB | 2024-07-10 | https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/pm-hasina-reiterates-call-china-help-repatriate-rohingyas-myanmar  
  Claim: Hasina pushed a diplomatic track for Rohingya repatriation through talks with Myanmar and support from China. This is one of the better 2024 examples of a nonviolent international-influence or security objective being pursued through diplomacy. | Question IDs: 8B.10

## Negative evidence

- **Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina secures fourth straight term in vote boycotted by main opposition** | Reuters | 2024-01-08 | https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-pm-sheikh-hasina-secures-fourth-straight-term-in-vote-boycotted-by-main-opposition/1914659/  
  Claim: Reuters said the BNP boycotted after Hasina refused to resign and allow a neutral authority to run the election. This is strong evidence of power-consolidation through control of the electoral apparatus rather than broader contestability. | Question IDs: 8B.10

- **Financial Sector and Fiscal Policy Reforms Will Help Bangladesh Sustain Strong Growth** | World Bank | 2024-04-02 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/02/financial-sector-and-fiscal-policy-reforms-will-help-bangladesh-sustain-strong-growth-despite-strong-growth-south-asia-r  
  Claim: The World Bank said inflation was eroding purchasing power, reserves were under pressure, and investment was being dampened by tight liquidity, import restrictions, and high costs. This is negative evidence on whether the regime was actually improving the conditions it claimed to manage. | Question IDs: 8B.10

- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain** | Reuters | 2024-07-22 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153  
  Claim: Reuters reported Hasina blaming opposition parties for the violence while keeping the curfew in place after internet shutdowns and military deployment. This shows coercive crisis management and blame-shifting, not movement toward a durable or safer program. | Question IDs: 8B.10

- **Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina resigns, interim government to be formed** | Reuters | 2024-08-05 | https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-pm-sheikh-hasina-resigns-interim-government-to-be-formed/2208572/  
  Claim: Reuters reported Hasina resigned and fled the country as an interim government was formed. That is the clearest sign that the year ended in collapse, not in closer realization of a durable ruler program. | Question IDs: 8B.10

- **Bangladesh: Back UN Investigation into Grave Abuses** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-26 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/26/bangladesh-back-un-investigation-grave-abuses  
  Claim: HRW said the crackdown on protests was the deadliest in Bangladesh’s recent history, with at least 440 killed and many injuries tied to excessive force and Awami League-linked violence. This is strong evidence that Hasina’s governing method worsened legitimacy and control conditions rather than strengthening them. | Question IDs: 8B.10

## Synthesis

The best reading is **mixed early, negative overall**. Hasina did make some visible progress on parts of her revealed program in 2024: procurement digitization, IMF-backed stabilization, some technocratic planning, and a few diplomatic / humanitarian initiatives. But those gains were narrow and fragile. The decisive 2024 story is that election legitimacy was already weak in January, the July crisis pushed the state into coercive shutdowns and deadly force, and the year ended with her fleeing and an interim government taking over. That means she was **not closer by the end of 2024** to a durable ideological, policy, or power-consolidation program than she was at the start.
